Looking at the image, I can identify the following key features:

- **Affected plant part**: Sugarcane leaves clustered at the crown/base of the plant
- **Color pattern**: Leaves show extensive browning/necrosis (tan to dark brown), with **distinctly pale/yellowish midribs** visible along the length of the leaves
- **Texture/pattern**: Leaves are desiccated and dried, with necrosis appearing to progress from tip to base
- **Plant structure**: Leaves are clustered at the crown; the plant appears stunted with shortened internodes
- **Stem**: Some reddish coloration visible on stem bases

**Matching against symptom descriptions:**

- **Yellow_Leaf** matches strongly: yellowing specifically of the midribs, necrosis progressing from tip to base, clustering of leaves at the crown, and complete leaf drying/stunting in severe cases — all clearly visible.
- **Leaf_Scald** is ruled out: no visible white pencil-line stripe extending from midrib to margin.
- **Sugarcane_Mosaic_Virus / Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv**: No mosaic/interveinal streak pattern present; this is generalized necrosis.
- **Grassy_Shoot**: No bushy grass-like tillering appearance.
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: No wrinkled/twisted young leaves or knife-cut stem lesions.

The severe yellowing of midribs progressed to complete leaf necrosis and drying, with crown-clustered leaves and stunted growth is the hallmark of **Yellow_Leaf** disease in its advanced stage.
